solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hard to avoid in merciless villain’s garment? (5-7)

blocks.note: a habit is a monk's or nun's robe
a garment belonging to Ming the Merciless, the Flash Gordon villain, is one FOR MING

annotation.surface: A question about what a cruel villain would choose to wear.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is doing the work: the villain's garment is a habit FOR MING, Ming the Merciless being the tyrant of the Flash Gordon comics.
annotation.definitionFit: Something habit-forming, like a drug, is hard to give up or avoid.

entries.clue: Physicist’s important piece bearing fruit (7)

definitions.note: The definition is possessive; read 'Physicist's' as 'Physicist is', with the rest of the clue what he is.

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece bearing another carries it on top

blocks.note: the haw is the hawthorn's berry

annotation.surface: A physicist's prized possession is something that bears fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer the king bears the haw by sitting under it, so HAW is written first.
annotation.definitionFit: Stephen Hawking was the British theoretical physicist.

entries.clue: Increasingly cruel to older British, appallingly (14)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged appallingly, i.e. badly

annotation.surface: Someone is being ever more cruel to elderly Britons, which is appalling.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue barring the definition is fodder, including 'to', which the surface uses as an ordinary preposition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bloodthirstier is the comparative of bloodthirsty, so more cruel than before.

entries.clue: Subject and object of the selectors, briefly (5)

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: what selectors aim to do is TO PICK (a team)

annotation.surface: A remark about team selectors being both the subject and the target of attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Object' is aim, not the grammatical object: the selectors' object is to pick.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the subject of a talk or essay is its theme.

entries.clue: Miscreant dying perhaps to open present (8)

indicators.note: END goes into OFFER, opening it up

blocks.note: dying is one kind of end; 'perhaps' flags an example

annotation.surface: A villain on his deathbed is about to unwrap a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but works as the verb 'offer'.
annotation.definitionFit: An offender is a wrongdoer, which is what a miscreant is.

entries.clue: Miss artificially produced sounds (4)

indicators.note: the answer sounds like the word clued

annotation.surface: A woman makes fake noises.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'produced sounds' together, but 'produced' belongs with 'artificially' and 'sounds' is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned sense: a maid, or maiden, was a young unmarried woman, the same person addressed as Miss.

entries.clue: Training series that’s raised a genius with figures (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting a word writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: a run is a series; raised, it becomes NUR
Alan Turing, the mathematician and codebreaker

annotation.surface: A training course that has produced a mathematical prodigy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With figures' reads as having a good physique, but means with numbers: Turing was a mathematician.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: rearing and educating a child both come under the noun, as in 'nature versus nurture'.

entries.clue: Determined to catch late night election procedure — but failing? (3,3,3,5)

blocks.note: if you are out for something you are set on getting it
British votes are counted overnight after polls close

annotation.surface: Someone is keen to stay up for the election count, yet fading.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is loose: a boxer out for the count has failed to get up.
annotation.definitionFit: A boxer out for the count has been knocked out, so has failed in the bout.

entries.clue: Spare space, as we see it, outside pub (6)

indicators.note: SKY goes outside INN, around it

blocks.note: the sky is the part of space we see from the ground

annotation.surface: Spare room is found outside a pub, apparently.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like extra, as in spare space, but here it is the adjective for thin, as in a spare frame.
annotation.definitionFit: A spare figure is lean, which is skinny.

entries.clue: Cheer health organisation work (5)

annotation.surface: A cheer for the work of a health body.
annotation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, the Latin word for a numbered musical work.
annotation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of joy, a cheer.

entries.clue: Outlaw in long distance run, I gather (5,4)

indicators.note: 'in' places the words before it inside the word after: R and I end up in FAR

blocks.note: a long way away is far
r = run, the cricket scoring abbreviation
a tuck gathers cloth into a fold

annotation.surface: A fugitive taking part in a long-distance race, the speaker reckons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I gather' looks like 'I understand', but I goes inside FAR and 'gather' is the needlework sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck was one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws.

entries.clue: Tend with cine reels to be needing some censorship? (8)

indicators.note: as a verb, to reel is to stagger unsteadily, so letters that reel lurch out of their order

annotation.surface: A projectionist looks after film reels that might need cutting by the censor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cine reels' reads as film spools, which suits censorship, but 'reels' is the verb telling TEND and CINE to stagger about.
annotation.definitionFit: Indecent material is the kind a censor would cut.

entries.clue: Diver coming out with pants just too short (6)

indicators.note: one letter short of complete, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: someone coming out with pants, short breaths, is puffing

annotation.surface: A swimmer emerges from the water in trunks that are a bit skimpy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'pants' underwear, and 'too short' a fashion complaint; pants here are gasps.
annotation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird that dives for fish.

entries.clue: Leave those with possessions to retain large share (2,6)

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so HAVES keeps L held inside it

blocks.note: the haves, as against the have-nots
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: An instruction to leave the wealthy holding most of the pie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large share' looks like one phrase; 'large' is L and 'share' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: splitting a bill fifty-fifty is sharing it.

entries.clue: Gentle creature on motorbike races a scooter (9)

blocks.note: the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man

annotation.surface: A mild-mannered animal riding a motorbike overtakes a scooter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a position word but supplies RE, and 'races' is a noun, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lambretta is an Italian motor scooter, beloved of 1960s Mods.

entries.clue: Subject of wartime graffiti: one line in city recalled (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places the words before it inside the word after: I and L end up in the city
the city is called back, written backwards

annotation.surface: A historian's note on a slogan chalked on walls during the war.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' applies only to the city, which is turned round before the other letters go in; 'one line' reads as a slogan but is two abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Kilroy was here', with a long-nosed face peering over a wall, was scrawled everywhere by Second World War servicemen.

entries.clue: Pilot quietly longing for somewhere to trade, unofficially (8)

blocks.note: to pilot a plane is to fly it

annotation.surface: An aviator privately wishes for an informal place to do business.
annotation.walkthrough: A flypitch is British slang for an unlicensed street trader's pitch, and 'unofficially' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A flypitch is a stall or spot used by an unlicensed street trader.

entries.clue: Shiny metal chain, see (6)

blocks.note: ch = chain, the old surveyor's measure of 22 yards
the Holy See is in Rome, the Pope's see

annotation.surface: A glittering metal chain for you to look at.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' sounds like 'look', but it is a bishop's see; the see of Rome belongs to the Pope.
annotation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plating, the bright shiny finish on car trim.

entries.clue: Bow Church concealing the sounds of its bells (6)

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide, and CE hides RING by wrapping round it

annotation.surface: The church at Bow, London, hides the sound of its bells.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is also the London district whose St Mary-le-Bow bells define a Cockney; here it is the verb, to bend low.
annotation.definitionFit: Older sense: to cringe once meant to bow or stoop servilely, before it came to mean flinching with embarrassment.

entries.clue: Florist primarily is trailing fashionable shop window item? (8)

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of Florist is taken

blocks.note: one who is trailing lags behind

annotation.surface: A florist puts a fashionable display piece in the shop window.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a loose definition: a flagship is a brand's showcase, whether a store or a product.
annotation.definitionFit: A flagship is the leading item a firm shows off, as a window display does.

entries.clue: Exercising power every twelve months, briefly becoming irritable (7)

indicators.note: abbreviated: YEAR is cut to Y

annotation.surface: Someone who wields power once a year and gets tetchy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exercising power' reads as one phrase about authority; it splits into PE and P.
annotation.definitionFit: A peppery person is hot-tempered and irritable.

entries.clue: Confine to broadcast as a series (2,4)

indicators.note: a word to be broadcast is spoken, so the answer sounds like it

blocks.note: to intern is to confine, as in wartime

annotation.surface: An instruction to restrict something to a broadcast serial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Series' suggests a TV serial, as does 'broadcast', but the definition means one after another.
annotation.definitionFit: Things done in turn happen one after another, as a series.

entries.clue: Busy checking progress of the career-minded? (5,3)

blocks.note: a busy is British slang for a police officer
cryptically, the career-minded are motorists careering along

annotation.surface: An ambitious office worker's progress being monitored by a busy boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career-minded' means inclined to career, drive too fast, not ambitious; and 'busy' is the British slang for a police officer.
annotation.definitionFit: A speed cop is a traffic policeman who stops speeding drivers.

entries.clue: Engaged in the writer’s revolutionary musical (5)

indicators.note: revolved, turned round, so read up the down answer

annotation.surface: A setter admits to working on a musical about a revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' fits the musical's subject, the Peróns of Argentina, but here it turns ATIVE round.
annotation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón.

entries.clue: Mount Juif Errant (4)

indicators.note: wandering, so the letters stray

annotation.surface: The Wandering Jew of legend, in French, climbs a mountain.
annotation.walkthrough: Le Juif errant is French for the Wandering Jew, so the surface is a bare title; 'errant' means wandering.
annotation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain.

entries.clue: Relative disquiet at EU grant (5-4)

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed

annotation.surface: A headline about comparative unease over a European Union subsidy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like an adjective qualifying 'disquiet'; it is the noun, a family member.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a parent's aunt is one kind of relative.

entries.clue: Get used to another union backing demos (5)

indicators.note: read the letters backwards
demonstrates, shows the answer within the words

blocks.note: the letters sit across anothER UNIon

annotation.surface: A second trade union supports protest marches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demos' looks like the protests a union backs; it is the verb, demonstrates.
annotation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to something unpleasant; to get used to it is to become inured.

entries.clue: A sweet little boy, I keep mum and dad’s score! (6,6)

blocks.note: sh! means keep quiet; to keep mum is to say nothing
a try is a score in rugby

annotation.surface: A child's proud announcement: the little lad stayed quiet and his dad scored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum and dad' looks like a pair of parents, but 'keep mum' is the phrase for staying silent.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in British usage a sweet can be any sweet food, and this flaky iced bun is one.
